description: A simple Python web app where phone-authenticated users create shareable Yes/No prediction contests, resolve answers as events happen, and view leaderboards.

services.name: Web application
services.description: Contest creation, entry, answer status, profile, and leaderboard pages.

services.name: Python application API
services.description: Authentication integration, authorization, contest lifecycle, scoring, and persistence.

questions.question: Which browser language should the web experience use?

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Simplest separate browser layer for a small Vercel-hosted app.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds type safety but slightly increases setup complexity.

questions.rationale: A small browser layer keeps the Python API straightforward while remaining compatible with Vercel.

questions.question: Should the UI be a separate browser frontend or server-rendered by the Python app?

options.label: Server-rendered pages with progressive enhancement
options.description: Simplest deployment and fewer moving parts; the Python app renders HTML.

options.label: Separate JavaScript single-page frontend
options.description: Richer client interactions but requires an additional frontend build and API integration.

questions.rationale: The user requested maximum simplicity and a Python web app on Vercel.

questions.question: Which language should power the application API?

options.label: Python
options.description: Requested language and a natural fit for a small Vercel Python serverless application.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: A Vercel-native alternative, but not the requested language.

questions.question: Which Python API framework should the application use?

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Azure serverless framework; it is not the natural deployment target for Vercel.

questions.rationale: Flask is a small, Vercel-compatible custom Python framework; FastAPI is an alternative if API-first behavior is preferred.

questions.question: Which data stores should the app use?

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Supabase PostgreSQL for profiles, contests, questions, answers, and scores.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: For uploaded files or media; not needed for the described MVP.

options.label: Redis cache
options.description: Optional cache; adds operational cost and complexity.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only for an app with no persistence.

questions.rationale: The user explicitly requested PostgreSQL on Supabase; no files or media are required.

questions.question: Should users sign in to use application API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Required for phone OTP, profiles, contest ownership, answer submission, and authorization.

options.label: No
options.description: Would prevent reliable ownership and private profile behavior.

questions.rationale: Phone SMS OTP authentication and user-owned contests are explicit requirements.

questions.question: Which SMS OTP approach should be used, balancing Supabase/Vercel simplicity and ongoing message cost?
questions.recommendedChoice: Supabase Auth phone OTP with a configured SMS provider

options.label: Supabase Auth phone OTP with a configured SMS provider
options.description: Keeps verification, sessions, and user identity together in Supabase; SMS provider fees still apply.

options.label: External SMS OTP service integrated by the Python app
options.description: More control over provider and cost, but adds credential, rate-limit, and session complexity.

questions.answer: Supabase Auth phone OTP with a configured SMS provider
questions.rationale: This is the simplest fit for Supabase PostgreSQL, but the provider and per-message cost need confirmation.

questions.question: Define the desired contest lifecycle, participation visibility, answer-locking rule, scoring rule, and tie behavior. A simple default is draft → open → locked/resolving → completed; one answer per question locks at contest close; each correct answer is one point; ties share the same rank.
questions.rationale: These choices materially affect authorization, database constraints, and leaderboard calculations.

questions.question: Specify profile visibility and contest access. A simple default is private phone numbers, public display name/username only, and unlisted contests accessible to anyone with the stable share URL.
questions.rationale: Stable shareable URLs require an explicit choice between unlisted access, membership, or public discovery.

questions.question: Confirm whether the MVP may use Vercel Python serverless execution, Supabase connection pooling/SSL, and environment secrets for Supabase and SMS configuration; avoid long-running jobs and local filesystem state.
questions.rationale: These are the simplest reliable deployment boundaries for Vercel plus Supabase.
